#01

Security Assessment and Ethical Hacking

Individual Assignment

Malware Attack Chain and Behavioural Detection

Shellcode Hooka Sysmon

A full malware attack chain using advanced techniques such as shellcode injection, evasive loaders built with Hooka, and Parent PID spoofing to bypass protections. The defensive side is examined with Sysmon and System Informer, showing detection relies on behavioural analysis (e.g. RWX memory) rather than file signatures.

Buffer Overflow Exploitation with GDB

Buffer Overflow GDB Exploit Dev

Analysis and exploitation of a buffer-overflow vulnerability in checker.c. Using GDB, the flaw in process_input was located and the offset computed to build a payload that redirects execution to the hidden win() function.

An end-to-end penetration test of a legacy Windows Server 2003 following the Cyber Kill Chain: reconnaissance with Nmap, remote code execution against IIS 6.0 via Metasploit, privilege escalation to SYSTEM, and password cracking with John the Ripper.

A successful DNS spoofing attack using the Man-in-the-Middle technique with Ettercap on Kali Linux. Through ARP poisoning and the dns_spoof plugin, the victim's traffic was redirected from the legitimate DNS server to an attacker-controlled Apache web server and a forged page.

iptables ModSecurity WAF

Individual Assignment

Dumpster Diving: Physical Security and Social Engineering

Social Engineering Physical Security OSINT

A presentation on dumpster diving as a reconnaissance technique in cybersecurity — physically searching an organisation's or individual's discarded material to recover information usable in a security breach. #05

Wireless and Mobile Network Security

Individual Assignment

Android Pentesting: Insecure Local Storage

Android Apktool SQLite

Penetration testing and reverse engineering of two vulnerable Android apps to recover hidden flags, using Apktool to decode configuration files (e.g. AndroidManifest.xml) and Android Studio for dynamic exploration. Reveals insecure local storage, recovering flags from SQLite Write-Ahead Log files and Shared Preferences XML stored in plain text.

Preview & Download (PDF)
Individual Assignment

Android Login Bypass via Reverse Engineering

Frida Ghidra Smali

Bypassing Android authentication through three reverse-engineering methodologies: static Smali patching with JADX and APKTool, decompiling a native C/C++ library with Ghidra to defeat stack-string obfuscation and recover hard-coded credentials, and runtime memory manipulation with Frida. Demonstrates that client-side security through obscurity is unsafe and that server-side validation is essential.

Preview & Download (PDF)
Individual Assignment

IEEE 802.11 Frame Analysis in Monitor Mode

802.11 Monitor Mode Wireshark

Monitoring and analysis of wireless traffic at the Data Link Layer of IEEE 802.11. The wireless card is set to monitor mode on Kali Linux to capture raw frames, which are analysed in Wireshark to confirm the three frame categories (Management, Control, Data) via the Frame Control field, establishing the groundwork for active deauthentication attacks.

Preview & Download (PDF)
Individual Assignment

Deauthentication Attack and 4-Way Handshake Capture

Deauth aireplay-ng EAPOL

Moving from passive monitoring to active packet injection with a targeted deauthentication attack. Using airodump-ng to map the network (BSSID, channel) and aireplay-ng to inject forged management frames, the target is forced to disconnect and, on reconnection, its WPA/WPA2 authentication data (4-Way Handshake / EAPOL) is captured, a preparatory stage for full network compromise.

Individual Assignment

Cracking WEP with the PTW Method

WEP aircrack-ng RC4

Practical compromise of the WEP protocol, exposing its weaknesses in IV management and the RC4 cipher. A controlled testbed is built on Kali Linux with airbase-ng as a virtual access point; captured packets feed aircrack-ng using the PTW method, recovering the full 64-bit key from only ~15,000 IVs and proving WEP's inadequacy for modern networks.

Individual Assignment

Evil Twin Rogue Access Point Attack

Evil Twin Rogue AP RSNA

Analysis of IEEE 802.11 management frames (Beacon, Probe) and the 4-way handshake (RSNA) in Wireshark, followed by an active Layer-2 Evil Twin attack. By manually creating a rogue access point, the work demonstrates the protocol's inherent lack of AP authentication, which allows client devices to be successfully deceived.

Individual Assignment

WPS Attacks: Reaver and Pixie-Dust

WPS Reaver Pixie-Dust

Analysis of the architectural vulnerabilities of Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) on WPA2-PSK networks. Covers deauthentication to capture the 4-way handshake for an offline dictionary attack, brute-force with Reaver, and the Pixie-Dust technique exploiting weak nonce generation on certain chipsets, while showing how modern WPS Lockout defences block automated attempts.

Individual Assignment

WPA2 Vulnerabilities: Hole196, PMKID and KRACK

WPA2 PMKID KRACK

Evaluation of three critical WPA2 vulnerabilities in a Kali Linux testbed. Implements the Hole196 attack (an insider abusing the shared GTK for ARP spoofing and MitM to decrypt IoT camera traffic), the modern PMKID attack (hcxdumptool + Hashcat for offline password recovery), and analyses the KRACK key-reinstallation flaw via PCAP, showing how replaying Handshake Message 3 collapses the encryption.

Individual Assignment

Enterprise Wi-Fi Attack on EAP-PEAP (802.1X)

EAP-PEAP 802.1X hostapd-wpe

Implementation of an attack on the EAP-PEAP authentication method under IEEE 802.1X via a rogue access point on Kali Linux. Using kernel virtual interfaces (mac80211_hwsim) with hostapd-wpe to overcome hardware limits, it captures the client's encrypted MSCHAPv2 credentials, proving the risk in WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise networks when the server certificate is not strictly validated.

Individual Assignment

WPA2 vs WPA3 and Downgrade Attacks

WPA3 SAE Downgrade

A comparative security analysis of WPA2 and WPA3 on Kali Linux. A deauthentication attack on WPA2 captures the 4-Way Handshake for an offline dictionary attack, while WPA3's protections (Protected Management Frames, SAE/Dragonfly) are evaluated. Using Airgeddon, an Evil Twin exploits WPA3 Transition Mode to show how downgrade attacks can force devices onto older, vulnerable standards.

#06

Cyber Defense and Digital Forensics

Individual Assignment

Active Directory Penetration Testing to Domain Admin

Active Directory Golden Ticket DCSync

A black-box penetration test of an Active Directory environment following the attack lifecycle (enumeration, initial access, privilege escalation). Using Nmap, Impacket, PowerView and John the Ripper, the chain leverages AS-REP Roasting, ACL abuse (GenericAll) and a DCSync attack to extract the krbtgt key and forge a Golden Ticket, achieving full Domain Admin control of the Domain Controller.

Preview & Download (PDF)
Individual Assignment

Active Directory Kill-Chain via Shadow Credentials and Diamond Ticket

Shadow Credentials Diamond Ticket PKINIT

A full attack kill-chain escalating from an unprivileged domain user to full SYSTEM privileges on a Windows Server 2016 Domain Controller. Starting from exposed credentials in SMB shares, it exploits Shadow Credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink) to bypass PKINIT authentication, then uses DCSync and Pass-the-Hash to extract the krbtgt key and forge a stealthy Diamond Ticket with high OpSec resilience.

Disk Forensics Investigation with Autopsy

Autopsy Disk Forensics Registry

A digital forensics investigation of a disk image using Autopsy. Covers recovering the OS installation timeline, Windows Registry analysis, browser and USB artifacts, SHA-256 hash verification, and bookmarking evidence artifacts to answer a structured set of forensic questions.

Volatility Memory Forensics pslist

Analysis of a system memory dump using Volatility 3 on Linux. Reconstructs running processes and their PID/PPID relationships (pslist), extracts credential hashes (hashdump), and hunts for anomalies to reconstruct system activity at the moment of capture.

Legal Framework of Security and Privacy

Group Assignment

Spyware, Digital Constitutionalism and the AI Act (Pegasus + Predator)

Pegasus Predator AI Act

A legal and technical study of intrusive spyware such as Pegasus and Predator through the lens of digital constitutionalism. Examines zero-click infection mechanisms and the national and European framework on lifting communications privacy, and — through the Pegasus and Greek 'Predatorgate' case studies — argues (de lege ferenda) for a risk-based regulatory approach aligned with the EU AI Act.

Preview & Download (PDF)
Group Assignment

Spyware Technologies and Privacy by Design (FORCEDENTRY)

FORCEDENTRY Privacy by Design Zero Trust

A technical study of the evolution of spyware such as Pegasus and Predator into state-level cyberweapons, centred on the FORCEDENTRY zero-click attack against iMessage and the limits of perimeter defence and anti-forensics. Proposes a shift to Privacy by Design (ISO/IEC 29100, 27701) and the Zero Trust architectural design of an Electronic Health Record using RBAC and Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs).

Advanced Topics in Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence

Individual Assignment

AI-Powered Phishing Detection with ML and Heuristics

Machine Learning Phishing Explainable AI

An advanced phishing-detection system combining Machine Learning with heuristic rules. It adds targeted features (Feature Engineering) such as DGA detection via Shannon entropy, display-name spoofing and lure-term detection; compares classifiers (LinearSVC wins on TF-IDF), performs adversarial error analysis, and adds Explainable-AI risk-score breakdowns for transparent decisions.

View on GitHub Preview & Download (PDF)
Individual Assignment

Prompt Injection Benchmark and Defence for LLMs

LLM Prompt Injection Defense-in-Depth

A benchmark for evaluating and hardening Large Language Models against prompt injection. A realistic bank-support assistant with canary tokens auto-detects data leaks across 60 benign and adversarial tests in five attack families; a three-layer defence (input check, context separation, output filtering) is validated by ablation, driving attack success to zero, with an LLM-judge and cross-model comparison (Llama 3.1 8B vs Mistral 7B).

Individual Assignment

Hybrid Intrusion Detection System (Snort + ML)

IDS Snort Random Forest

Design and evaluation of a hybrid IDS combining signature-based detection with Machine Learning. In a testbed generating realistic attack traffic (SYN scans, ICMP floods, stealth web probes), custom Snort rules provide accuracy while supervised (Random Forest, Logistic Regression) and unsupervised (Isolation Forest) models improve recall; a weighted risk-scoring fusion reaches an F1-score of 0.926.

Individual Assignment

Zero-Trust Risk-Adaptive Access Control

Zero Trust Access Control Gradient Boosting

A risk-adaptive access-control engine built on Zero Trust, combining Machine Learning with deterministic rules. On synthetic enterprise logs simulating normal activity and attacks (Impossible Travel, Privilege Escalation, Bulk Data Spike), a hybrid of Gradient Boosting and Isolation Forest with hard safety rules reaches PR-AUC 0.942, and adds Responsible-AI explainability, fairness analysis and concept-drift simulation.

Individual Assignment

LLM-Enhanced SSH Honeypot and Attacker Analytics

Honeypot LLM Isolation Forest

Design and evaluation of an interactive SSH honeypot enriched with decoy artefacts generated by Large Language Models. A virtual filesystem and shell emulator run attack playbooks (reconnaissance, credential theft, lateral movement); sessions are clustered by engagement (K-means, Isolation Forest) and attacker intent classified (Random Forest), showing LLM-generated decoys are as convincing as manual ones while applying Responsible-AI isolation and data minimisation.

Group Assignment

ScamAI: Generative-AI Fraud Detection and Response

Generative AI Scambaiting Responsible AI

A group project presenting ScamAI, which combines Generative AI and Machine Learning against phishing/scamming. It works in two stages: passive detection of malicious messages via a Random Forest trained on 13,919 emails, and active scambaiting using LLM personas tailored to the scam type. Emphasises Responsible AI with output guardrails and prompt-injection defences, plus an ethical/legal analysis (GDPR, AI Act, NIS2).
